requirements.title: Payment allocation to highest-APR balance
requirements.given: Account has Purchase APR 22.99%, Cash Advance APR 27.99%, both with balances.
requirements.when: Make a payment greater than the minimum due.
requirements.then: excess above minimum applies first to the balance with the highest APR (cash advance).
requirements.failureMode: system applies excess to purchases first, or splits pro-rata.

requirements.title: Zero-balance bucket stops accruing interest
requirements.given: Cash advance balance is paid to exactly $0.00 mid-cycle.
requirements.when: Run interest accrual for remainder of the cycle.
requirements.then: no further interest accrues on the cash advance bucket for that cycle.
requirements.failureMode: system keeps a residual daily balance > 0 due to rounding and keeps charging interest.

requirements.title: Balance transfer fee classified correctly
requirements.given: 3% balance transfer fee applied on a $5,000 transfer.
requirements.when: Check which APR bucket the fee itself accrues interest under.
requirements.then: fee is added to the balance-transfer bucket, not treated as a purchase.
requirements.failureMode: fee silently posts to purchase APR bucket (usually higher, mischarges customer).

requirements.title: New purchase during active promo BT balance
requirements.given: Account has a 0% promotional balance-transfer balance and no prior purchase balance.
requirements.when: Make a new purchase.
requirements.then: new purchase accrues interest from transaction date since grace period is void when a non-promotional balance triggers it, unless issuer's specific policy differs — verify against issuer's own T&Cs.
requirements.failureMode: purchase incorrectly inherits 0% promo rate, or grace period incorrectly still applies.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Overpayment beyond total balance
requirements.given: Total balance across all buckets is $1,200.
requirements.when: Submit a payment of $1,500.
requirements.then: account reflects a $300 credit balance; no bucket goes negative in a way that generates phantom interest.
requirements.failureMode: negative balance in one bucket generates negative interest / credit interest bug, or payment is rejected silently.

requirements.title: Refund/credit posts to correct bucket
requirements.given: A purchase made under standard APR is refunded by the merchant.
requirements.when: Process merchant refund/credit.
requirements.then: credit reduces the purchase bucket balance and associated accrued interest is reversed proportionally.
requirements.failureMode: credit posts as a generic credit not tied to a bucket, average daily balance calc unaffected (customer overcharged).

requirements.title: Simultaneous same-day purchase and cash advance
requirements.given: Customer makes a purchase and a cash advance on the same calendar day.
requirements.when: Run end-of-day balance calculation.
requirements.then: each transaction accrues under its own APR bucket from its own posting date.
requirements.failureMode: system merges same-day transactions into one bucket using the last-written APR.

requirements.title: Chargeback/dispute freezes interest accrual
requirements.given: Customer disputes a purchase transaction; issuer opens a chargeback.
requirements.when: Advance billing cycles while dispute is open.
requirements.then: disputed amount is excluded from interest-bearing balance per Reg Z billing error rules.
requirements.failureMode: disputed amount continues accruing interest while under investigation.

requirements.title: Minimum payment exactly equals amount due
requirements.given: Minimum payment due is $35.00 across two buckets.
requirements.when: Pay exactly $35.00.
requirements.then: no 'excess' allocation logic triggers; payment applied per issuer's stated minimum-payment allocation method.
requirements.failureMode: system still attempts highest-APR allocation logic on the minimum itself, contradicting Reg Z (only required for amounts ABOVE minimum).

requirements.title: Promotional purchase APR alongside standard purchase APR
requirements.given: Two purchase sub-buckets exist: promo-rate purchases (12.99%) and standard-rate purchases (24.99%), same 'purchase' category.
requirements.when: Make payment above minimum.
requirements.then: excess allocates to the standard-rate purchase sub-bucket first (higher APR), even though both are nominally 'purchases.'.
requirements.failureMode: system treats all purchases as one bucket and ignores the APR sub-split.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Fee-only transaction with no APR bucket
requirements.given: A late fee or annual fee posts with no natural APR bucket assignment.
requirements.when: Run interest accrual and payment allocation.
requirements.then: issuer's documented default bucket (commonly purchase APR) is applied consistently.
requirements.failureMode: fee floats unassigned and is silently excluded from balance entirely, understating amount owed.

requirements.title: Refunds correctly distinguish between a revolving (interest-bearing) balance and an interest-free installment-plan balance on the same account
requirements.driver: CFPB Supervisory Highlights, Spring 2022 (Issue 26) — named deceptive-practices/refund-handling examination finding
requirements.given: Account has both a standard revolving balance that accrues interest and a separate fixed monthly installment plan balance that is interest-free for its duration (a structure some issuers offer for large purchases).
requirements.when: Process a merchant refund/credit for a purchase that was originally financed under the interest-free installment plan.
requirements.then: refund is applied to reduce the correct balance (the installment-plan balance) and is processed per the specific terms of the credit card agreement governing that plan — not defaulted to the general revolving balance.
requirements.failureMode: system processes the refund against the wrong balance type (e.g., applies it to the revolving balance instead of the installment plan, or vice versa), which CFPB examiners specifically found issuers doing incorrectly, along with inadequately disclosing the pre-conditions for the interest-free financing itself.

requirements.title: Promo APR expires on exact final day
requirements.given: 12-month 0% promo starting Jan 15; today is day 365 (Jan 14 next year, inclusive count depends on issuer definition).
requirements.when: Compute interest for a transaction dated on the last promotional day vs the first day after.
requirements.then: last promotional day still 0%; the following day reverts to standard APR — boundary matches issuer's documented definition of the promo period.
requirements.failureMode: off-by-one: promo ends one day early or one day late versus disclosed terms.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Deferred-interest full balance paid one day late
requirements.given: Deferred-interest promo: 'no interest if paid in full within 18 months.' Balance is $1 short at the deadline.
requirements.when: Reach deadline with $1.00 remaining unpaid.
requirements.then: full retroactive interest for the entire promo period applies to the ENTIRE original balance, per the specific deferred-interest terms disclosed — verify this matches disclosure exactly (not more, not less).
requirements.failureMode: system charges retroactive interest on only the unpaid $1, OR fails to charge retroactive interest at all.

requirements.title: Deferred-interest balance paid in full exactly on deadline
requirements.given: Same deferred-interest promo as above; balance reaches $0.00 exactly on the deadline date.
requirements.when: Verify no retroactive interest posts.
requirements.then: zero retroactive interest charged; account transitions cleanly to standard APR going forward.
requirements.failureMode: system still charges retroactive interest due to a '>=' vs '>' comparison bug on the deadline date.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: New purchase made on promo's last valid day
requirements.given: 0% purchase APR promo ends today.
requirements.when: Post a new purchase transaction today, before cutoff time.
requirements.then: transaction receives the promotional rate since it posted within the promo window.
requirements.failureMode: batch job processing order causes the transaction to be evaluated after the promo flag was already flipped off for the day.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Promo rate applied only to eligible balance type
requirements.given: Promo is a 0% BALANCE TRANSFER APR only; purchase APR is standard.
requirements.when: Make a new purchase after the promo is active.
requirements.then: purchase accrues standard APR; only the transferred balance gets 0%.
requirements.failureMode: system applies 0% to the whole account balance instead of just the balance-transfer bucket.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Multiple stacked promos on same account
requirements.given: Customer has a 0% purchase promo (6 months) and a separate 3.99% BT promo (18 months), started on different dates.
requirements.when: Advance time so one promo expires while the other is still active.
requirements.then: each promo tracks its own independent expiration and reverts only its own bucket to standard APR.
requirements.failureMode: expiration of one promo incorrectly resets both to standard APR, or resets the wrong bucket.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Promo APR canceled due to late payment (if terms allow)
requirements.given: Promo terms state promotional rate is forfeited if a payment is 60+ days late.
requirements.when: Simulate a payment 61 days late during the promo period.
requirements.then: promo APR is revoked per disclosed terms and normal (or penalty, if applicable) APR applies going forward, not retroactively unless deferred-interest terms specifically say so.
requirements.failureMode: system retroactively applies standard APR to the whole promo period when terms didn't authorize retroactive application, or fails to revoke the promo at all.

requirements.title: Promo APR floor/negative rate edge case
requirements.given: Promotional APR is set to exactly 0.00%.
requirements.when: Run interest accrual calculation.
requirements.then: interest charged is exactly $0.00, not a negative number or a rounding artifact like $0.01.
requirements.failureMode: floating point rounding produces a nonzero interest charge on a 0% balance.

requirements.title: Promo expiration mid-billing-cycle (not aligned to statement date)
requirements.given: Promo expires on the 10th of the month; billing cycle runs 1st–末(end of month).
requirements.when: Compute interest for that billing cycle.
requirements.then: days 1–10 accrue at promo rate, days 11–end accrue at standard rate (blended interest calculation), reflected accurately on the statement.
requirements.failureMode: system applies a single APR for the whole cycle (either all-promo or all-standard) instead of blending by day.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Promo re-enrollment after prior promo already used
requirements.given: Customer completed a 0% BT promo 3 months ago; a new promo offer is issued.
requirements.when: Attempt to enroll and use the new promo.
requirements.then: system applies issuer's own eligibility rules (commonly restricting reuse within a time window) consistently and blocks or allows accordingly.
requirements.failureMode: prior promo history isn't checked, letting ineligible re-enrollment succeed (or incorrectly blocking eligible customers).
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Payment allocation cannot be steered away from an expiring deferred-interest balance
requirements.given: Customer has a deferred-interest promotional balance nearing its expiration deadline and a separate standard-rate balance; customer pays an amount above the minimum specifically intending to pay off the promo balance in time.
requirements.when: Verify where the excess payment is actually allocated when the customer has requested (or the system defaults to) directing it toward the expiring promo balance.
requirements.then: excess payment is applied to the promotional balance as requested/expected, giving the customer a genuine opportunity to avoid retroactive interest — consistent with CFPB enforcement precedent against allocating payments in a way that causes deferred interest to be incurred.
requirements.failureMode: system allocates the excess payment to the higher-APR standard balance (or otherwise away from the promo balance) even when the customer requested otherwise, causing the promo deadline to be missed and retroactive interest to be charged — the specific pattern CFPB has previously pursued as an unfair practice.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: 59 vs 60 vs 61 days late boundary
requirements.given: Payment due date has passed with no payment received.
requirements.when: Advance the clock to exactly day 59, day 60, and day 61 past due; check penalty APR status at each.
requirements.then: penalty APR does not trigger before day 60; triggers on/after day 60 per Reg Z minimum threshold and issuer's disclosed terms.
requirements.failureMode: penalty APR triggers early (e.g., 30 days) or the day-count is off by one at the boundary.

requirements.title: Penalty APR applies only to new transactions unless 60+ days late
requirements.given: Account becomes 45 days late (not yet 60).
requirements.when: Check whether any penalty-rate condition applies at 45 days, and to which balances if issuer has a policy for shorter delinquency.
requirements.then: no penalty APR applied at 45 days (below the 60-day floor) unless a different specific default condition in the cardholder agreement is met and disclosed.
requirements.failureMode: system incorrectly applies penalty APR to the entire existing balance before the 60-day threshold.

requirements.title: 6-month cure period restores standard APR
requirements.given: Penalty APR is in effect; customer makes 6 consecutive on-time minimum (or greater) payments.
requirements.when: Simulate 6 consecutive on-time payments post-penalty.
requirements.then: standard APR is restored starting the billing cycle after the 6th on-time payment, per Reg Z cure provisions.
requirements.failureMode: cure never triggers, or triggers after the wrong number of payments, or resets prematurely if only 5 payments were made.

requirements.title: Cure period broken by a single late/short payment
requirements.given: Customer makes 4 consecutive on-time payments during cure tracking, then pays $1 short of minimum in month 5.
requirements.when: Check cure counter after the short payment.
requirements.then: cure counter resets to zero; customer must restart the 6-consecutive-payment sequence.
requirements.failureMode: system doesn't detect the underpayment (off by a small amount) and lets cure counter continue incrementing.

requirements.title: Payment exactly equal to minimum counts as 'on time'
requirements.given: Customer's payment equals the minimum due to the exact cent, received before the due date/time cutoff.
requirements.when: Evaluate whether this counts toward the cure sequence.
requirements.then: counts as a qualifying on-time payment.
requirements.failureMode: system requires payment to exceed minimum by some margin, disqualifying exact-minimum payments incorrectly.

requirements.title: Penalty APR interacts with active promo APR
requirements.given: Customer has an active 0% purchase promo AND becomes 61 days late.
requirements.when: Trigger penalty APR conditions.
requirements.then: system applies issuer's documented precedence rule (commonly: penalty APR does not override a promo unless cardholder agreement explicitly allows), consistently reflected on statement.
requirements.failureMode: ambiguous precedence leads to conflicting APRs being applied to the same balance simultaneously, or silent default with no audit trail.

requirements.title: Grace-period/courtesy days before 'late' status counts
requirements.given: Payment due date is the 1st; issuer's system has an internal processing/courtesy buffer of 1–2 days before marking 'late.'.
requirements.when: Make payment on day 2 after due date.
requirements.then: 'Days late' counter for penalty APR purposes starts from the true contractual due date, not from when the internal courtesy buffer expires (unless disclosed otherwise).
requirements.failureMode: courtesy buffer silently shifts the entire 60-day penalty clock, delaying penalty APR beyond what's disclosed — or the reverse, applying it early.

requirements.title: Penalty APR notice/advance notice requirement
requirements.given: Penalty APR is about to be applied to an existing balance (60+ days late scenario).
requirements.when: Check that a 45-day advance change-in-terms notice was generated where required.
requirements.then: required notice is generated and logged before the new rate takes effect on qualifying balances.
requirements.failureMode: penalty rate applies to the system's interest calc before/without the required notice being sent.

requirements.title: Multiple delinquency events don't stack penalty APR
requirements.given: Customer goes 65 days late, cures via 6 on-time payments, then goes 65 days late again 2 months later.
requirements.when: Verify penalty APR is reapplied correctly on the second delinquency, not compounded or double-applied.
requirements.then: second delinquency independently re-triggers standard penalty APR terms (not a harsher escalated rate unless disclosed).
requirements.failureMode: system stacks or escalates the penalty rate beyond the single disclosed penalty APR.

requirements.title: Partial payment received exactly on due date at cutoff time
requirements.given: Payment posts at 11:59:59 PM in the issuer's stated time zone on the due date, for the full minimum.
requirements.when: Evaluate 'on-time' status.
requirements.then: counted as on-time; day-late counter starts at 0.
requirements.failureMode: time zone mismatch (e.g., system uses UTC internally vs issuer's disclosed local time zone) misclassifies this as 1 day late.

requirements.title: Penalty APR cap / usury ceiling check
requirements.given: State usury law or card agreement specifies a maximum permissible APR.
requirements.when: Attempt to apply a penalty APR that would exceed the disclosed maximum.
requirements.then: system caps at the disclosed/legal maximum and flags the conflict rather than silently applying an over-limit rate.
requirements.failureMode: system applies the raw configured penalty rate even when it exceeds the disclosed ceiling.

requirements.title: Prime rate change applies prospectively only
requirements.given: Variable APR = Prime + margin. Prime rate changes mid-billing-cycle.
requirements.when: Recompute interest for the cycle in which prime changed.
requirements.then: days before the change use old prime-based APR; days after use new rate (blended calculation), matching disclosed methodology.
requirements.failureMode: system retroactively applies new rate to the entire cycle, or ignores the change until the next cycle when terms require immediate application.
requirements.blockedOn: billing cycle segmentation or a live index feed

requirements.title: Index feed returns stale/missing data
requirements.given: External prime-rate/index feed fails to update or returns null for a scheduled date.
requirements.when: Trigger interest calculation while index data is stale or missing.
requirements.then: system falls back to last known-good verified value and flags for manual review; never silently uses $0, null-as-zero, or an uninitialized variable.
requirements.failureMode: aPR calculation silently computes using a null/zero index, producing 0% or a huge erroneous rate.

requirements.title: Rate floor and ceiling enforcement
requirements.given: Cardholder agreement specifies APR floor of 9.99% and ceiling of 29.99% regardless of index movement.
requirements.when: Simulate an index value that would push computed APR below the floor or above the ceiling.
requirements.then: aPR is clamped to the disclosed floor/ceiling.
requirements.failureMode: system applies the raw computed rate outside the disclosed bounds.

requirements.title: Index rate change during an active promo
requirements.given: Customer has 0% promo; prime rate changes during the promo period.
requirements.when: Recompute rates for both the promo bucket and any standard-rate bucket.
requirements.then: promo bucket remains unaffected by index changes (fixed 0%); only standard-rate/variable buckets adjust.
requirements.failureMode: index change incorrectly perturbs the promotional bucket's rate.
requirements.blockedOn: billing cycle segmentation or a live index feed

requirements.title: Negative index value or extreme index spike
requirements.given: Index feed returns an anomalous value (negative, or 10x normal).
requirements.when: Run interest calculation with the anomalous index value.
requirements.then: system validates against a sane range, rejects/flags the anomaly, and does not apply it silently.
requirements.failureMode: system computes and applies a nonsensical APR (negative interest credited to customer, or extreme overcharge) without validation.

requirements.title: Rate change notice timing for variable-rate accounts
requirements.given: Prime-indexed variable rate changes due to index movement (not issuer discretion).
requirements.when: Verify whether a change-in-terms notice is required/sent.
requirements.then: system correctly applies the Reg Z carve-out: index-tied changes generally don't require the 45-day notice, but the new rate/method must still appear on the next statement.
requirements.failureMode: system either sends unnecessary notices causing customer confusion, or fails to disclose the new rate on the next statement.

requirements.title: Rounding of index + margin to disclosed precision
requirements.given: Prime = 8.25%, margin = 14.740%, computed APR = 22.99% (issuer discloses rates to 2 decimal places).
requirements.when: Compute and store the resulting APR.
requirements.then: stored/displayed APR rounds per issuer's disclosed rounding method (commonly nearest 0.01%), consistently between calculation and disclosure.
requirements.failureMode: internal calculation uses full floating-point precision while the disclosed/displayed rate is truncated differently, causing a mismatch between charged and disclosed APR.

requirements.title: Multiple index changes within a single cycle
requirements.given: Prime rate changes twice within one 30-day billing cycle.
requirements.when: Recompute interest, applying both rate segments correctly.
requirements.then: interest is calculated as three properly-bounded rate segments (pre-first-change, between changes, post-second-change) summing to the correct total.
requirements.failureMode: system only picks up the last rate change and applies it to the whole cycle, or misses one of the segments entirely.
requirements.blockedOn: billing cycle segmentation or a live index feed

requirements.title: System does not blindly trust a benchmark index without integrity/reasonableness checks
requirements.driver: In re: Interest Rate Swap Antitrust Litigation-style benchmark-rate claims; pending Oct. 2025 federal class action alleging WSJ Prime Rate coordination among major banks (allegations unproven)
requirements.given: The account's variable APR is tied to a published benchmark rate (e.g., a prime rate reported by a financial news source) that the issuer does not control.
requirements.when: Verify what safeguards exist if the published benchmark itself were later disputed, restated, or alleged to be unreliable (a real, currently-litigated allegation exists that several major banks' prime-rate submissions were coordinated in a way that could have inflated the published rate used across the industry — the underlying claim is unproven and contested, but it illustrates that index inputs are not infallible).
requirements.then: system logs the index value and source actually used for every rate calculation (not just the resulting APR), so that if a benchmark is ever restated or successfully challenged, affected accounts and periods can be precisely identified and corrected — an auditable input trail, not just an auditable output.
requirements.failureMode: system stores only the final computed APR with no retained record of which index value/source/date was used to derive it, making retroactive correction across potentially millions of accounts operationally infeasible if a benchmark integrity issue is later established.
requirements.blockedOn: billing cycle segmentation or a live index feed

requirements.title: Margin/spread changes are tracked and disclosed separately from index-driven APR movement
requirements.driver: CFPB Consumer Credit Card Market Report, Dec. 2025 — market-wide APR-margin finding
requirements.given: An issuer's variable APR = published index (e.g., prime) + a margin the issuer sets. The index itself moves independently of the margin.
requirements.when: Verify the system tracks and can report the margin component separately from the index component, and that any margin increase (as opposed to an index-driven change) goes through the same change-in-terms notice treatment as any other discretionary rate increase.
requirements.then: margin changes are distinguishable from index changes in the system's records and trigger appropriate disclosure regardless of what the index is doing concurrently — so a margin increase can't be procedurally hidden inside a period of flat or falling index rates.
requirements.failureMode: system stores and monitors only the final blended APR, with no separate record of the margin component over time — meaning a margin increase during a period of falling index rates could produce a stable or even declining disclosed APR, masking a discretionary rate increase that independently warranted its own notice. (CFPB's Dec. 2025 Credit CARD Act Report found the spread between the prime rate and actual charged APRs at its widest level since the Bureau began tracking it — a market-wide pattern worth specifically testing for at the system level.).

requirements.title: 365 vs 360 day divisor consistency
requirements.given: Issuer's cardholder agreement specifies daily periodic rate = APR / 365.
requirements.when: Inspect the actual divisor used in the interest engine.
requirements.then: divisor matches disclosed value (365) consistently across every calculation path in the codebase.
requirements.failureMode: some code path uses /360 (a banking-convention holdover) causing systematic overcharge/undercharge vs disclosure.

requirements.title: Leap year day-count handling
requirements.given: Billing cycle spans Feb 29 in a leap year.
requirements.when: Compute daily periodic rate and total days in cycle including Feb 29.
requirements.then: 366 total days in the year is correctly reflected if the issuer's methodology is 'APR/actual days in year'; if issuer uses a fixed 365 divisor per their agreement, Feb 29 still accrues a normal day's interest without being dropped or double-counted.
requirements.failureMode: system drops Feb 29 from the day count entirely, or double-counts it, or errors/crashes on the date.

requirements.title: Penny-level rounding accumulation over 12 cycles
requirements.given: Run the same $1,000 balance at a fixed APR through 12 consecutive monthly cycles with no payments.
requirements.when: Sum interest charged across all 12 cycles; compare to a precise (non-rounded) reference calculation.
requirements.then: cumulative rounding difference is within 1 cent of the precise reference (rounding per-cycle, not compounding rounding error).
requirements.failureMode: systematic rounding bias (always rounds up, or rounds the wrong number of decimal places before storing) causes measurable drift over many cycles.

requirements.title: Average Daily Balance with mid-cycle payment
requirements.given: Balance starts at $2,000; a $500 payment posts on day 15 of a 30-day cycle.
requirements.when: Compute Average Daily Balance for the cycle.
requirements.then: aDB = weighted average reflecting $2,000 for 14 days and $1,500 for 16 days (or issuer's exact documented method), matching disclosed methodology exactly.
requirements.failureMode: system uses simple start/end average instead of true daily weighting, or misplaces the payment by one day (off-by-one in day-count).

requirements.title: New transaction posted same day as payment
requirements.given: On day 15, a $500 payment posts AND a $200 purchase posts.
requirements.when: Compute the balance used for that specific day in the ADB calculation.
requirements.then: order of same-day postings follows issuer's documented sequencing (commonly payments-before-purchases) consistently, matching what's disclosed.
requirements.failureMode: posting order is nondeterministic (depends on processing batch order / race condition) so the same day's inputs produce different ADB on different runs.

requirements.title: Interest-on-interest (compounding) frequency
requirements.given: Cardholder agreement discloses daily compounding of interest.
requirements.when: Verify unpaid interest from prior days is added to the principal for calculating the next day's interest within the SAME cycle.
requirements.then: interest compounds daily as disclosed; total cycle interest matches a true daily-compounding reference calculation.
requirements.failureMode: system actually applies simple (non-compounding) interest despite disclosing daily compounding, or vice versa — undercharging or overcharging vs. disclosure.

requirements.title: Zero-day billing cycle / same-day account closure
requirements.given: Account is opened and closed (or a rate change and cycle end coincide) on the same calendar day.
requirements.when: Run interest calculation for that degenerate cycle.
requirements.then: system handles a zero or single-day cycle gracefully with correct pro-rated interest, no division-by-zero.
requirements.failureMode: divide-by-zero error, or negative days computed, or the interest engine throws an unhandled exception.

requirements.title: Rounding direction (round-half-up vs round-half-even/banker's rounding)
requirements.given: A daily interest calculation lands exactly on a half-cent (e.g., $0.125).
requirements.when: Check which rounding rule is applied and whether it's consistent across the whole system.
requirements.then: one documented rounding rule (e.g., round-half-up) is applied consistently everywhere interest is rounded.
requirements.failureMode: different code paths (accrual engine vs statement generator vs payoff quote) use different rounding rules, producing mismatched figures for the 'same' number.

requirements.title: Interest calculation on a balance that goes negative intraday
requirements.given: A large refund posts mid-cycle, temporarily driving the purchase-bucket balance negative before a new purchase re-establishes a positive balance later the same cycle.
requirements.when: Compute ADB across the cycle.
requirements.then: negative daily balances are treated as $0 for interest-accrual purposes (customer isn't charged negative-balance 'interest' unless issuer explicitly pays credit interest) or handled per documented policy.
requirements.failureMode: negative values are summed directly into the ADB, artificially lowering the average and thus interest — or system errors out.

requirements.title: Statement period boundary transaction (11:59 PM cutoff)
requirements.given: A purchase posts at 11:59:58 PM local time on the last day of a billing cycle.
requirements.when: Verify which cycle the transaction is assigned to.
requirements.then: transaction is assigned to the correct cycle based on issuer's documented cutoff time and time zone.
requirements.failureMode: time zone handling bug (e.g., server in UTC, issuer discloses Eastern Time) shifts the transaction into the wrong cycle.

requirements.title: Extremely small balance rounds to zero interest
requirements.given: Balance is $0.03 at a 24.99% APR for one day.
requirements.when: Compute daily interest.
requirements.then: interest computed to sub-cent precision internally, only rounded for display/charging at the final statement step (not rounded to $0.00 prematurely mid-calculation).
requirements.failureMode: interest engine rounds to the nearest cent at EVERY daily step, causing legitimate small interest amounts to vanish (systematic undercharge) or accumulate incorrectly.
requirements.blockedOn: product configuration and disclosed rate ranges

requirements.title: Grace period revoked after carrying $1 forward
requirements.given: Previous statement balance was NOT paid in full (e.g., $1.00 left unpaid) by the due date.
requirements.when: Make new purchases in the current cycle and compute when interest starts accruing on them.
requirements.then: grace period is revoked; new purchases accrue interest from their transaction date, not the statement date.
requirements.failureMode: system still grants a grace period on new purchases despite the unpaid prior balance.

requirements.title: Grace period restored after paying in full
requirements.given: Prior cycle balance was carried; customer then pays the full NEW statement balance by its due date.
requirements.when: Check grace period status for the following cycle.
requirements.then: grace period is restored for the next cycle's new purchases.
requirements.failureMode: system treats grace period as permanently revoked once lost, never restoring it despite full payment.
requirements.blockedOn: product configuration and disclosed rate ranges

requirements.title: Grace period only applies to purchases, not cash advances
requirements.given: Cash advances typically accrue interest immediately with no grace period, per most cardholder agreements.
requirements.when: Take a cash advance while the account otherwise qualifies for a purchase grace period.
requirements.then: cash advance accrues interest from the transaction date regardless of purchase grace-period status.
requirements.failureMode: system incorrectly extends the purchase grace period to the cash advance balance.

requirements.title: Partial payment of prior balance still revokes grace
requirements.given: Prior balance was $500; customer pays $499.99, missing full payment by one cent.
requirements.when: Compute grace period status for new purchases.
requirements.then: grace period revoked (any amount less than full balance revokes it, per standard terms).
requirements.failureMode: system has a rounding tolerance bug that treats 'close enough' as paid in full.

requirements.title: New account first statement grace period
requirements.given: Brand-new account, first billing cycle, no prior balance exists.
requirements.when: Make a purchase and check interest accrual before the first due date.
requirements.then: grace period applies by default (no prior balance to have been unpaid), per standard terms.
requirements.failureMode: system requires a 'previous full payment' history that doesn't exist yet, incorrectly denying grace period on the very first cycle.

requirements.title: Grace period interaction with autopay for exact statement balance
requirements.given: Autopay is configured to pay the full statement balance automatically each cycle.
requirements.when: Verify grace period is maintained across cycles when autopay executes successfully.
requirements.then: grace period maintained as long as autopay successfully pays in full and on time.
requirements.failureMode: autopay payment posts one day after the due date due to processing delay, and system doesn't reconcile this against the grace-period eligibility check.

requirements.title: Grace period status displayed to customer matches actual calculation
requirements.given: Account is in a state where grace period was just revoked this cycle.
requirements.when: Check what the customer-facing statement/UI displays versus what the interest engine actually applied.
requirements.then: displayed grace-period status matches the engine's actual behavior exactly.
requirements.failureMode: uI/statement shows 'grace period active' while the backend engine already started charging interest from transaction date (or vice versa).

requirements.title: Grace period on a balance-transfer-only account with no purchases
requirements.given: Account has only a promotional balance-transfer balance; no purchase activity at all.
requirements.when: Make a first purchase while the BT balance is still outstanding.
requirements.then: system applies issuer's specific documented rule for this scenario (varies by issuer — some revoke purchase grace when ANY balance is carried, others don't).
requirements.failureMode: undefined/inconsistent behavior because this combination wasn't handled, defaulting to whatever the code path happens to do.

requirements.title: Displayed APR matches APR used in calculation
requirements.given: Standard purchase APR is configured as 24.99% in the rate engine.
requirements.when: Cross-check the APR value printed on the generated statement against the value actually used by the interest-accrual engine for that cycle.
requirements.then: both values match exactly.
requirements.failureMode: statement-generation service reads from a cached/stale rate table while the accrual engine already updated to a new rate, so the two disagree.

requirements.title: Effective APR disclosure matches nominal APR calculation
requirements.given: Statement must show 'Interest Charge Calculation' box with APR and corresponding periodic interest charged.
requirements.when: Verify the effective APR shown (interest charged / balance * appropriate factor) reconciles with the nominal APR disclosed elsewhere.
requirements.then: effective and nominal APR reconcile within expected rounding tolerance.
requirements.failureMode: a calculation bug elsewhere (e.g., wrong day-count) causes the two disclosed figures on the SAME statement to contradict each other.

requirements.title: Minimum payment warning box uses correct APR
requirements.given: Statement includes the 'minimum payment warning' showing payoff time/total if only minimums are paid.
requirements.when: Verify this projection uses the account's actual current APR(s), including any active penalty or promo rates.
requirements.then: projection uses live, correct APR(s) for each balance bucket.
requirements.failureMode: projection uses a hardcoded default APR unrelated to the customer's actual current rate.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Rate change disclosed on statement before it takes effect
requirements.given: A rate change (e.g., prime-indexed adjustment) will take effect next cycle.
requirements.when: Check current statement for advance disclosure of the upcoming rate.
requirements.then: statement discloses the change per Reg Z timing requirements.
requirements.failureMode: rate silently changes with no corresponding statement disclosure trail.

requirements.title: Historical statements remain immutable after a rate correction
requirements.given: Issuer discovers and fixes an APR calculation bug affecting past cycles.
requirements.when: Check whether historical statement records/PDFs are altered retroactively versus a proper corrected-statement/adjustment process.
requirements.then: original statements remain as historical record; correction appears as a new adjustment entry with its own audit trail.
requirements.failureMode: system overwrites historical statement data in place, destroying the audit trail of what was actually disclosed to the customer at the time.

requirements.title: Multiple APRs each separately itemized when balances exist in more than one bucket
requirements.given: Account has purchase, cash advance, and promo balances simultaneously.
requirements.when: Check the interest charge calculation box on the statement.
requirements.then: each APR/balance type is itemized as its own line, per Reg Z, not combined into a single blended figure.
requirements.failureMode: statement collapses multiple APRs into one blended average APR, obscuring the actual rate applied to each balance type.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: 45-day advance notice for significant rate change
requirements.given: Issuer wants to raise the standard purchase APR for a customer with no delinquency trigger (discretionary change).
requirements.when: Simulate the rate-change workflow and check for the 45-day notice.
requirements.then: change is blocked/queued until 45-day notice period has elapsed, notice is logged as sent.
requirements.failureMode: system allows the rate change to take effect immediately without checking for or generating the required notice.

requirements.title: First-year rate lock for new accounts
requirements.given: New account opened less than 12 months ago; no penalty/index/promo-expiration condition applies.
requirements.when: Attempt a discretionary APR increase within the first 12 months.
requirements.then: system blocks the increase — Reg Z generally prohibits raising APR in the first year except for specific enumerated reasons.
requirements.failureMode: system allows an arbitrary discretionary rate increase inside the 12-month protected window.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Ability-to-pay / reevaluation for rate increases doesn't bypass APR limits
requirements.given: A rate increase is proposed as part of a required periodic account reevaluation.
requirements.when: Verify the new rate still respects any applicable caps/floors and required notices.
requirements.then: increase still goes through full change-in-terms and notice workflow like any other increase.
requirements.failureMode: reevaluation-triggered changes are coded as a special path that skips the standard notice/disclosure checks.

requirements.title: State usury limits override configured APR where applicable
requirements.given: Card is issued to a resident of a state with a usury cap lower than the issuer's national standard rate (where state law isn't preempted).
requirements.when: Compute effective APR for that customer.
requirements.then: system applies the correct rate per applicable law/preemption analysis for that customer's situation.
requirements.failureMode: system applies a single national rate table with no state-specific override capability at all.

requirements.title: Right to reject a rate increase and close account under old terms
requirements.given: Customer receives a 45-day notice of a discretionary rate increase and opts to reject it before it takes effect.
requirements.when: Simulate customer rejection within the notice window.
requirements.then: account is closed to new charges but existing balance continues to amortize at the OLD APR, per Reg Z opt-out rights.
requirements.failureMode: system applies the new (higher) rate anyway despite the timely rejection, or fails to preserve the old rate on the remaining balance.

requirements.title: Reg Z billing error / dispute interest suspension window
requirements.given: Customer submits a written billing error notice.
requirements.when: Advance time through the required investigation period.
requirements.then: disputed amount and related interest are held/suspended per the required timeline until resolved.
requirements.failureMode: system continues normal interest accrual and negative reporting on the disputed amount during the protected investigation window.

requirements.title: Military/SCRA interest rate cap
requirements.given: Cardholder qualifies for Servicemembers Civil Relief Act protections (active duty status verified).
requirements.when: Compute APR with SCRA cap applied (commonly 6%).
requirements.then: aPR is capped at the legally required maximum for the protected period.
requirements.failureMode: system has no SCRA override mechanism and continues applying standard/penalty APR.

requirements.title: Co-branded/private-label card different rate rules
requirements.given: Card is a retail co-branded card with different promotional/deferred-interest rules than the issuer's general-purpose cards.
requirements.when: Run the same APR test scenarios against the co-branded product configuration.
requirements.then: product-specific rules apply correctly and don't leak logic from the general-purpose card configuration.
requirements.failureMode: shared code path applies general-purpose card defaults to the co-branded product, contradicting its specific disclosed terms.

requirements.title: Account closure doesn't stop legitimately accrued interest disclosure
requirements.given: Customer closes the account with a remaining balance.
requirements.when: Continue billing cycles post-closure until balance is paid off.
requirements.then: interest continues to accrue and be disclosed on statements per the terms in effect at closure; APR doesn't silently change upon closure.
requirements.failureMode: system either stops generating statements (hiding accruing interest) or silently applies a different 'closed account' rate not disclosed to the customer.

requirements.title: Daylight Saving Time transition during a billing cycle
requirements.given: Billing cycle spans a DST 'spring forward' or 'fall back' transition date.
requirements.when: Compute day-count for interest accrual across the transition.
requirements.then: day-count logic uses calendar days, unaffected by the 23-hour or 25-hour clock day during DST transition.
requirements.failureMode: system computes elapsed time using timestamp deltas (e.g., hours/86400) instead of calendar-day differences, producing a fractional day error on the transition date.

requirements.title: Transaction posted across UTC date line vs local business date
requirements.given: Card is used internationally; transaction timestamp in UTC falls on a different calendar date than the issuer's local business-day convention.
requirements.when: Assign the transaction to a billing cycle and interest-accrual date.
requirements.then: transaction is assigned per the issuer's documented convention (commonly cardholder's local time or issuer's processing time zone), consistently.
requirements.failureMode: transaction date varies depending on which service in the pipeline evaluates it (some using UTC, others local), causing inconsistent bucket assignment.

requirements.title: Due date falling on a weekend or holiday
requirements.given: Payment due date calculated falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or bank holiday.
requirements.when: Check due-date and grace-period/late-fee logic.
requirements.then: reg Z requires that if a due date isn't a business day, a payment received the next business day can't be treated as late.
requirements.failureMode: system marks a payment received the next business day as late, incorrectly triggering fees/penalty-APR-clock start.

requirements.title: Billing cycle length varies (28 vs 30 vs 31 vs 30/31-day months)
requirements.given: Statement cycles run on a fixed 'same day of month' schedule across months of different lengths.
requirements.when: Compute daily periodic rate application across a 28-day February cycle vs a 31-day March cycle.
requirements.then: interest correctly reflects the actual number of days in each specific cycle, not a fixed assumed cycle length.
requirements.failureMode: system assumes a fixed 30-day cycle length for all months, over/undercharging interest depending on actual month length.

requirements.title: Year-end / New Year's Eve cycle boundary
requirements.given: Billing cycle end falls on Dec 31, with next cycle starting Jan 1 (year change).
requirements.when: Verify interest calculation, statement generation, and any annual fee logic handle the year transition correctly.
requirements.then: no off-by-one or date-parsing errors across the year boundary; annual APR-related fee calculations (if any) apply to the correct year.
requirements.failureMode: date library defaults or string-parsing bugs miscalculate day differences across the year boundary.

requirements.title: Leap second / system clock skew during batch interest job
requirements.given: Nightly interest-accrual batch job runs across a system clock adjustment or NTP resync.
requirements.when: Simulate clock skew during the batch run window.
requirements.then: batch job uses a consistent logical 'as-of' date for the entire run, unaffected by mid-run clock adjustments.
requirements.failureMode: some records get processed with 'yesterday's' date and others with 'today's' date within the same batch run, double-counting or skipping a day.

requirements.title: Simultaneous payment and purchase transactions
requirements.given: A payment and a new purchase are submitted within milliseconds of each other, near a billing cycle cutoff.
requirements.when: Submit both concurrently and inspect final balance/bucket state.
requirements.then: both transactions apply deterministically and correctly regardless of arrival order/timing (idempotent, properly sequenced processing).
requirements.failureMode: race condition causes one transaction to be lost, double-applied, or applied against a stale balance snapshot.

requirements.title: Rate change job running concurrently with interest-accrual job
requirements.given: A scheduled APR update (e.g., prime rate change) and the nightly interest-accrual batch job are scheduled to run at the same time.
requirements.when: Trigger both processes concurrently.
requirements.then: interest accrual uses a consistent, correctly-versioned rate for each day (no partial application of the new rate to already-processed days).
requirements.failureMode: accrual job reads the rate table mid-update, applying the new rate to some already-processed cycle-days and the old rate to others inconsistently.

requirements.title: Duplicate payment submission (double-click / retry)
requirements.given: Customer's payment request is submitted twice due to a client-side retry or double-click, within the same second.
requirements.when: Submit the duplicate payment scenario.
requirements.then: system detects and deduplicates (idempotency key or similar), applying the payment exactly once.
requirements.failureMode: payment is applied twice, incorrectly reducing balance and potentially affecting grace-period/cure-sequence logic.

requirements.title: Statement generation running during an in-flight interest correction
requirements.given: A correction to a miscalculated interest charge is being applied at the same moment the monthly statement generation job runs.
requirements.when: Trigger both processes concurrently for the same account.
requirements.then: statement either waits for the correction to complete or clearly reflects a consistent pre-correction or post-correction state — never a partially-applied mix.
requirements.failureMode: statement captures a partially-applied correction, showing inconsistent/impossible numbers (e.g., interest charge doesn't match the balance change).

requirements.title: Penalty APR trigger and cure-sequence check racing on the same payment
requirements.given: A payment simultaneously (a) counts toward the 60-day-late penalty trigger evaluation and (b) counts toward an in-progress 6-payment cure sequence.
requirements.when: Process the payment and check both evaluations.
requirements.then: both evaluations read a consistent, correctly-ordered view of payment history (proper locking/transaction isolation).
requirements.failureMode: race condition lets one evaluation see the payment and the other miss it, producing contradictory account states (e.g., simultaneously 'in cure' and 'newly penalized').

requirements.title: High-volume end-of-cycle batch processing order dependency
requirements.given: Thousands of accounts hit cycle-end interest calculation in the same batch window, including this test account.
requirements.when: Verify this account's result is identical regardless of its position/order in the batch queue.
requirements.then: result is deterministic and independent of batch processing order.
requirements.failureMode: shared mutable state (e.g., a global rate cache being updated mid-batch) causes accounts processed later in the batch to get different results than accounts processed earlier, for what should be the same rate.

requirements.title: Manual override supersedes calculated standard rate
requirements.given: CSR/retention team applies a manual APR override (e.g., 15.99% retention offer) on an account whose system-calculated standard APR is 24.99%.
requirements.when: Run the nightly interest-accrual job for the account.
requirements.then: the override rate is used for accrual, not the underlying calculated rate, for as long as the override is active.
requirements.failureMode: accrual engine reads the base rate table directly and ignores the override flag/record entirely.

requirements.title: Override auto-expires and reverts cleanly
requirements.given: A temporary override (e.g., 6-month hardship rate of 9.99%) has an explicit expiration date.
requirements.when: Advance time past the override's expiration date without any manual action.
requirements.then: rate automatically reverts to whatever the underlying calculated rate would be at that point (standard, variable, or penalty — whichever legitimately applies), with no manual step required.
requirements.failureMode: override never expires (rate 'sticks' permanently), or expires but leaves a stale/frozen rate instead of correctly recalculating.

requirements.title: Override precedence vs penalty APR trigger
requirements.given: Account has an active retention override (15.99%) and separately becomes 65 days delinquent.
requirements.when: Trigger the penalty APR condition while the override is still within its validity window.
requirements.then: system applies issuer's documented precedence rule consistently (e.g., delinquency legitimately breaks a courtesy override, per the override's own terms) and logs which rule won.
requirements.failureMode: override and penalty APR both silently try to apply, and whichever was written to the database last (a race, not a business rule) wins.
requirements.blockedOn: override expiry dates and authorisation records

requirements.title: Override scoped to a single balance bucket, not the whole account
requirements.given: Override is documented as applying only to the purchase-APR bucket; cash-advance APR is untouched.
requirements.when: Verify cash-advance interest accrual is unaffected by the purchase-bucket override.
requirements.then: cash-advance bucket continues accruing at its own unmodified rate.
requirements.failureMode: override implementation is account-level only and incorrectly discounts every balance bucket.
requirements.blockedOn: override expiry dates and authorisation records

requirements.title: Override audit trail captures who/why/when
requirements.given: A CSR applies a manual rate override through the servicing tool.
requirements.when: Inspect the account's audit log after the override is applied.
requirements.then: log records the authorized user ID, reason code, old rate, new rate, effective date, and expiration (immutable record).
requirements.failureMode: override changes the rate but leaves no audit record, or the record can be edited/deleted after the fact.
requirements.blockedOn: override expiry dates and authorisation records

requirements.title: Unauthorized override attempt is blocked
requirements.given: A user account without override-granting permissions attempts to apply a manual APR override via an API call or internal tool.
requirements.when: Submit the override request with an under-privileged credential.
requirements.then: request is rejected and logged as a denied/unauthorized attempt.
requirements.failureMode: permission check only exists in the UI layer; the underlying API/service accepts the override regardless of caller's actual authorization level.
requirements.blockedOn: override expiry dates and authorisation records

requirements.title: Override vs active promotional APR — which wins
requirements.given: Account has an active 0% promotional purchase APR AND a CSR applies a 'goodwill' 12.99% override on the same bucket.
requirements.when: Compute the rate actually used for accrual.
requirements.then: system applies a defined precedence (commonly: the lower of the two, or promo takes precedence since it's contractually disclosed to the customer) and applies it consistently, not arbitrarily.
requirements.failureMode: both rates are 'active' in the data model with no tie-breaking logic, and the accrual job picks whichever row it reads last.

requirements.title: Override does not retroactively re-rate already-billed cycles
requirements.given: A CSR applies an override today; several prior billing cycles have already been calculated and disclosed under the old rate.
requirements.when: Verify prior, already-issued statements are not silently recalculated.
requirements.then: override applies prospectively from its effective date only; historical statements stand unless an explicit backdated adjustment is separately authorized and logged.
requirements.failureMode: system recalculates the entire account history under the new override rate, producing statement figures that don't match what was actually disclosed at the time.

requirements.title: Two overlapping overrides from different programs
requirements.given: Account qualifies for both a hardship program override (11.99%) and a loyalty/retention override (13.99%) applied by different teams in the same week.
requirements.when: Both overrides are submitted for the same balance bucket.
requirements.then: system detects the conflict and applies a defined resolution rule (e.g., most-recent-effective-date, or most-favorable-to-customer, per policy), not both simultaneously.
requirements.failureMode: system stores both as 'active' with no conflict detection, and behavior becomes dependent on read order / cache state.

requirements.title: Override reverts to penalty APR (not standard) if that's what underlying state requires
requirements.given: A temporary hardship override expires while the account is, independently, still within an active uncured 65-day delinquency.
requirements.when: Advance time past override expiration with delinquency still unresolved.
requirements.then: rate reverts to the correctly-applicable penalty APR (since that's the legitimate underlying state), not blindly back to the pre-override standard APR.
requirements.failureMode: system has a single 'previous rate' field it restores to on expiration, ignoring whatever should legitimately apply now.
requirements.blockedOn: override expiry dates and authorisation records

requirements.title: Override amount exceeds/violates disclosed floor or ceiling
requirements.given: A CSR attempts to key in an override rate of 45% (above the disclosed contractual/legal ceiling) or -2% (below zero).
requirements.when: Submit the out-of-bounds override value through the servicing tool.
requirements.then: system validates against configured floor/ceiling and rejects the entry with a clear error.
requirements.failureMode: system accepts and applies any numeric value typed in with no bounds validation.
requirements.blockedOn: override expiry dates and authorisation records

requirements.title: Promised debt/interest forgiveness under a settlement or hardship program is actually applied in the system, not just represented to the customer
requirements.driver: Illustrative precedent: multi-agency credit card enforcement action (2012) involving unfulfilled debt-forgiveness/settlement promises
requirements.given: Customer is offered a hardship or debt-settlement arrangement promising a specific dollar amount or percentage of accrued interest/balance will be waived or forgiven if certain conditions are met (e.g., a lump-sum payment or a completed payment plan).
requirements.when: Verify that once the customer meets the stated conditions, the promised interest/balance amount is actually canceled in the system of record — not merely referenced in a customer-facing letter while the underlying ledger still reflects the original, unforgiven balance.
requirements.then: the waived amount is actually removed from the account's outstanding balance and future interest stops accruing on it, matching exactly what was represented to the customer in writing.
requirements.failureMode: system sends the customer a forgiveness confirmation (satisfying a marketing/CS workflow) without a corresponding, verified write-down in the core ledger, so the account continues quietly accruing interest on a balance the customer was told no longer exists — echoing a real enforcement pattern where card issuers were found to promise debt forgiveness that was not actually honored in their systems.
requirements.blockedOn: override expiry dates and authorisation records

requirements.title: Prime rate increase does not raise an active SCRA-capped rate
requirements.given: Cardholder has an approved SCRA request; effective APR is capped at 6% on pre-service debt. Prime rate subsequently rises, which would normally push the variable APR above 6%.
requirements.when: Simulate a prime-rate increase during the SCRA-active period and run interest accrual.
requirements.then: rate charged remains capped at 6% (or the disclosed legal cap) regardless of the prime rate movement — the index change has no effect while SCRA is active.
requirements.failureMode: variable-rate recalculation job overwrites the SCRA cap flag with the new prime-indexed rate, silently breaking the legal protection.

requirements.title: Prime rate decrease during SCRA — customer gets the LOWER of computed rate or 6% cap
requirements.given: SCRA cap is active at 6%. Prime rate falls enough that the normal variable-rate formula (prime + margin) would compute to 4.5%, which is below the 6% cap.
requirements.when: Recompute the applicable rate.
requirements.then: customer is charged the lower of the two — 4.5% — since the SCRA cap is a ceiling, not a fixed rate; it should never raise a rate that would otherwise be lower.
requirements.failureMode: system treats 6% as a flat override rate rather than a ceiling, overcharging the customer 1.5 points versus what the standard formula would have produced.

requirements.title: SCRA cap applies to pre-service debt, not new post-activation charges
requirements.given: Cardholder enters active duty with an existing $3,000 balance, then makes a new $500 purchase after their active-duty start date.
requirements.when: Compute interest separately on the pre-service $3,000 and the post-activation $500.
requirements.then: system applies issuer's correct interpretation (commonly: the 6% cap covers debt incurred before military service began; new post-activation charges may be handled differently per issuer policy and disclosed terms — verify against current guidance, as some issuers extend the cap account-wide).
requirements.failureMode: system applies a single account-wide flag with no distinction by transaction date, either uniformly undercharging or uniformly failing to cap the pre-service balance.

requirements.title: SCRA cap overrides penalty APR regardless of delinquency
requirements.given: Cardholder has an active SCRA cap AND independently becomes 65 days delinquent, which would normally trigger penalty APR.
requirements.when: Trigger the penalty APR delinquency condition while SCRA cap is active.
requirements.then: the 6% legal cap takes precedence over penalty APR — SCRA protection cannot be overridden by an internal business rule like delinquency-triggered rate escalation.
requirements.failureMode: penalty-APR trigger logic runs independently of the SCRA-cap check and overwrites the capped rate with the penalty rate.

requirements.title: Retroactive forgiveness of interest charged before SCRA request was processed
requirements.given: Servicemember's active-duty start date is June 1; SCRA request is submitted and approved on June 20, after two billing cycles already charged standard/variable APR.
requirements.when: Process the approved SCRA request and check historical interest correction.
requirements.then: interest in excess of 6% charged from the June 1 active-duty start date forward (even before the request was processed) is identified and refunded/credited, per SCRA's retroactive-to-eligibility-date requirement.
requirements.failureMode: system only caps the rate prospectively from the approval date (June 20) forward, failing to correct the two cycles of overcharged interest between June 1 and June 20.

requirements.title: SCRA protection ends — reversion requires proper notice and correct rate
requirements.given: Servicemember's active-duty period ends; SCRA cap eligibility expires.
requirements.when: Advance time past the documented end-of-service date.
requirements.then: rate reverts to the correctly-applicable current rate (standard or variable, reflecting any prime-rate movement that occurred during the protected period) with appropriate customer notice of the reversion, not silently.
requirements.failureMode: system reverts to whatever rate was on file before SCRA was ever applied (stale/pre-protection rate) instead of the correct current rate, or reverts with no customer notice at all.

requirements.title: SCRA cap applies to interest rate only, not principal or fees
requirements.given: Account has an active SCRA cap; a late fee and an annual fee also post during the protected period.
requirements.when: Verify which charges the 6% cap is applied to.
requirements.then: only the interest-rate component is capped; principal balance and any legitimately-assessed fees are unaffected by the interest-rate protection (fee waivers, if any, are a separate SCRA provision and should be tracked independently).
requirements.failureMode: system either caps unrelated fee amounts as if they were interest, or fails to apply any SCRA-related fee provisions the issuer has separately committed to.
requirements.blockedOn: product configuration and disclosed rate ranges

requirements.title: Multiple, non-contiguous active-duty periods tracked independently
requirements.given: Servicemember has two separate active-duty periods on the same account (e.g., deployed, returned, redeployed a year later), each requiring its own SCRA request.
requirements.when: Simulate both periods with a gap of standard-rate billing in between.
requirements.then: each active-duty period's cap start/end dates are tracked independently; the gap period correctly bills at the standard/variable rate; the second period correctly re-triggers the cap without depending on stale state from the first.
requirements.failureMode: system has a single boolean 'SCRA active' flag with one start/end date pair, unable to represent a second, later period correctly — or auto-reapplies stale first-period dates.

requirements.title: Joint account: SCRA cap scope when co-applicant is not on active duty
requirements.given: Account has two cardholders (joint or authorized user); only one is the qualifying servicemember on active duty.
requirements.when: Apply the SCRA request and check which portion of the account's rate is capped.
requirements.then: system applies the issuer's documented and legally-correct policy consistently (this varies — verify against current guidance and the issuer's own policy — but the behavior must be intentional and consistent, not accidental).
requirements.failureMode: system either caps the whole joint account with no clear policy basis, or fails to apply any protection at all because the automated eligibility check only looks at the primary account holder field.

requirements.title: SCRA cap does not raise an already-lower promotional rate
requirements.given: Cardholder has an active 0% promotional purchase APR at the same time their SCRA request is approved (cap would be 6%).
requirements.when: Compute the rate actually applied.
requirements.then: customer continues to receive the lower 0% promotional rate — the SCRA cap is a ceiling and must never be used to raise a rate that is already below it.
requirements.failureMode: system treats an approved SCRA request as forcibly setting the rate to exactly 6%, overriding and canceling the more favorable 0% promo — actively harming the protected customer.

requirements.title: SCRA eligibility re-verification does not silently lapse the cap
requirements.given: Issuer's policy requires periodic re-verification of active-duty status (e.g., annually) to keep the cap in place.
requirements.when: Advance time past a re-verification checkpoint without any re-verification event occurring.
requirements.then: system flags the account for re-verification and does not remove the protection while re-verification is pending; any removal requires a positive determination that eligibility has actually ended, plus proper notice.
requirements.failureMode: cap silently expires the moment a re-verification date passes, reverting to standard/variable APR (and possibly penalty APR) even though the servicemember is still actively serving.

requirements.title: APR disclosed within permitted accuracy tolerance
requirements.given: System calculates and discloses an APR of 24.99% on the account-opening disclosure (Schumer box) using the actuarial method.
requirements.when: Independently compute the APR from the actual finance charge and balance figures the system produces, and compare to the disclosed 24.99%.
requirements.then: disclosed APR is within the TILA/Reg Z permitted tolerance (generally 1/8 of 1 percentage point for regular transactions) of the actuarially-computed rate.
requirements.failureMode: system's disclosed APR and its own finance-charge-derived effective APR diverge by more than the permitted tolerance, meaning the disclosure itself is inaccurate under TILA.

requirements.title: Account-opening disclosures delivered before first transaction
requirements.given: A new applicant is approved and a physical/digital card is issued. Check the sequence of events: disclosure delivery timestamp vs.
requirements.when: first transaction timestamp.
requirements.then: full initial TILA disclosures (APR, fees, grace period, balance computation method) are delivered before or at account opening, never after the first transaction has already posted.
requirements.failureMode: system allows card activation and a first purchase to complete before the disclosure document has actually been generated/sent, creating a sequencing violation.

requirements.title: Finance charge components correctly classified
requirements.given: Account has interest charges, a cash-advance fee, and a foreign-transaction fee in the same cycle.
requirements.when: Verify which charges are included in the disclosed 'finance charge' figure per TILA's definition versus itemized separately as 'other fees.'.
requirements.then: each charge is classified per Reg Z's definition of finance charge (e.g., interest and certain transaction fees are finance charges; others are separately itemized), and the statement math reconciles.
requirements.failureMode: system either lumps a non-finance-charge fee into the finance charge total (inflating disclosed APR-related figures) or omits a true finance-charge component, understating it.

requirements.title: Solicitation/application ('Schumer box') matches system-configured rate table
requirements.given: Marketing sends a pre-approved offer with a Schumer box stating 'Purchase APR: 19.99%–29.99%, based on creditworthiness.'.
requirements.when: Cross-check the Schumer box range against the actual APR values the underwriting/rate engine is configured to assign.
requirements.then: the disclosed range fully bounds every APR the system can actually assign to an approved applicant for that product.
requirements.failureMode: rate engine has been reconfigured (e.g., a new higher tier added) without the Schumer box being updated, so some approved customers receive a rate outside the range they were shown.

requirements.title: Deferred-interest promo includes required 'how it works' explanation
requirements.given: A deferred-interest 0% promotional offer is presented to the customer (in-app, mail, or point-of-sale).
requirements.when: Check the offer content for the specific required explanation of how deferred interest works, including that interest accrues from the purchase date and is charged retroactively if not paid in full by the deadline.
requirements.then: required explanatory language is present and matches the actual system behavior (see Promotional-APR test cases).
requirements.failureMode: marketing copy simply says '0% for 18 months' without the required deferred-interest mechanics disclosure, and/or the disclosed mechanics don't match what the interest engine actually does.
requirements.blockedOn: promo periods with start and end dates

requirements.title: Corrected disclosure reissued after a detected calculation error
requirements.given: An APR calculation bug is discovered and fixed; the bug affected disclosed APRs on account-opening documents for a cohort of accounts.
requirements.when: Verify the remediation workflow for affected accounts.
requirements.then: corrected disclosures are reissued to affected customers, and any resulting overcharge is refunded, with the whole remediation logged.
requirements.failureMode: system fix is deployed silently going forward with no backward-looking remediation process for already-affected accounts/disclosures.

requirements.title: Minimum finance charge disclosed and applied consistently
requirements.given: Cardholder agreement specifies a $0.50 minimum finance charge whenever any interest is owed for the cycle.
requirements.when: Compute a scenario where calculated interest would be $0.30 (below the minimum).
requirements.then: system charges exactly $0.50 (the disclosed minimum), not the raw calculated $0.30, and this minimum-charge rule itself was disclosed at account opening.
requirements.failureMode: system charges the raw $0.30 calculated amount, ignoring the disclosed minimum finance charge, or applies an undisclosed minimum.
requirements.blockedOn: account lifecycle dates and product conversion

requirements.title: Periodic statement includes complete Reg Z 1026.7 content set
requirements.given: Standard monthly statement is generated for an account with a balance.
requirements.when: Check statement content against the full Reg Z 1026.7 required-content list: previous balance, transactions, fees, interest charged (itemized by type), APR(s), balance computation method identified, closing balance, payment due date, minimum payment.
requirements.then: all required elements are present and internally consistent with each other (e.g., previous balance + transactions − payments + fees + interest = new balance, exactly).
requirements.failureMode: one or more required elements is missing, mislabeled, or the reconciliation math doesn't tie out due to a rounding/sequencing bug elsewhere in the pipeline.

requirements.title: Correct calculation regime (open-end tolerance vs. actuarial method/U.S. Rule) is applied to the correct balance type
requirements.driver: Reg Z 1026.14 (open-end tolerance) vs. Appendix J to Part 1026 (actuarial method/U.S. Rule for closed-end-like calculations)
requirements.given: A card product has a standard revolving (open-end) balance governed by §1026.14's disclosure-tolerance framework, and also offers an embedded fixed-payment installment-plan feature for large purchases that behaves more like closed-end credit. Verify the system applies §1026.14's open-end tolerance rules to the revolving balance, and separately applies the actuarial method or U.S.
requirements.when: Rule (per Appendix J) correctly to the installment-plan feature — not the same single framework blindly applied to both.
requirements.then: each balance type is evaluated under the calculation/disclosure regime that actually applies to it, since open-end and closed-end-like features are governed by materially different rules that were never designed to be interchangeable.
requirements.failureMode: system was originally built for a purely revolving product and, when an installment-plan feature was later bolted on, reused the open-end tolerance/calculation logic for it as well — applying the wrong regulatory framework to a feature that functions like closed-end credit.

requirements.title: Actuarial method and U.S. Rule are not mixed inconsistently for the same installment-plan feature
requirements.driver: Reg Z 1026.22(a) and Appendix J — both methods permitted, but must be applied consistently, not blended
requirements.given: A card's installment-plan feature uses one of the two TILA-permitted calculation methods (actuarial method or U.S. Rule); these methods can diverge specifically when a scheduled payment is missed or insufficient to cover the period's accrued finance charge. Verify the system consistently applies only ONE of the two methods for a given feature/product, particularly checking behavior in the missed/insufficient-payment scenario where the two methods' results diverge (the actuarial method capitalizes unpaid finance charge and compounds on it; the U.S.
requirements.when: Rule generally does not, in the same way).
requirements.then: one calculation method is chosen, documented, and applied consistently across every scenario for that feature — including the edge case of a missed or short payment, which is exactly where the two legally-permitted methods stop agreeing.
requirements.failureMode: system's normal-case calculation matches one method (e.g., actuarial) but its exception-handling code for missed/short payments was written independently and actually behaves like the other method (U.S. Rule) without anyone having decided that — an inconsistency invisible until a missed-payment scenario specifically exposes it.

requirements.title: The correct APR accuracy tolerance (1/8 point regular vs. wider tolerance for irregular schedules) is applied based on the actual payment/period structure
requirements.driver: Reg Z 1026.22(a)(4) and commentary — differing tolerances for regular vs. irregular transactions
requirements.given: One account has a completely regular payment schedule; another account has an irregular schedule (e.g., an odd first period from a mid-cycle account opening, or an odd first/final payment from a promotional structure).
requirements.when: Verify the system checks the disclosed APR against the correct tolerance for each account's actual schedule type — the standard 1/8 of 1 percentage point tolerance for regular transactions, versus the wider tolerance Reg Z permits specifically for irregular transactions.
requirements.then: tolerance checking is schedule-aware: regular accounts are held to the tighter 1/8-point standard, irregular accounts to the appropriately wider standard — matching what Reg Z actually specifies for each case.
requirements.failureMode: system applies a single hardcoded tolerance value to every account regardless of schedule regularity — if that value is the wider irregular-transaction tolerance, it could mask genuine disclosure inaccuracies on regular accounts that should be held to the tighter standard.

requirements.title: Promotional offer accurately represents deferred-interest risk
